name: Mariáš
summary: Three-player solo trick-taking Ace-Ten game from the King-Queen family, popular in Czech Republic and Slovakia.
rules_text: Mariáš is played with 32 cards A-10-K-O-U-9-8-7 ranking A,10,K,O,U,9,8,7 except in Betl/Durch. Three players receive cards, eldest hand views 7 cards and chooses trump, then receives 5 more and discards 2. The other two form a defending partnership. Play is 10 tricks. Must follow suit, must head the trick if able, must trump if cannot follow. Highest trump or highest of led suit wins. Winner leads and keeps won tricks in order. Aces and Tens are 10 each, last trick is 10, total 90. King+Ober of same suit in one hand is a marriage, worth 40 if trump else 20, if its holder wins a trick. Defenders can double with Flek, declarer can redouble. Hearts trump doubles stakes. Special contracts: Betl win no tricks, Durch win all tricks, 7 win last trick with lowest trump, 100 score 100+ points.
rating_reason: Three-player solo trick-taking, king-queen marriages scoring
